Sometimes it's important to realize there's more to statements than being "right" or "wrong". Some statements are even worse than that, and can be classified as "not even wrong". The idea goes back to Wolfgang Pauli, who famously quipped that a theory he was presented was so terrible it wasn't just no right, it wasn''t even wrong.

So what does this mean? An example makes it easy to understand.

2 + 2 = 4 is right

2 + 2 = 6 is wrong

2 + blue = kangaroo is "not even wrong"

There is no sensible way to classify the last statement as "wrong", because it would give it more legitimacy than it deserves. It is nonsense, clear and simple. You can't prove it wrong, because there isn't enough substance to prove anything. So if someone tells you nobody can prove their statement wrong, be very wary, because that doesn't mean it's right, it could very well be "not even wrong".
